qna.question: Name all four key changes of state.
What do we call the temperature at which a solid turns to liquid?
Why do scientists repeat measurements?
qna.answer: To check for errors and make their results more reliable.

qna.question: True or false — all changes of state are reversible.
qna.answer: True. Melting, freezing, evaporation and condensation can all be reversed.

qna.question: What does a higher melting point tell us about a material?
qna.answer: It needs more energy (heat) before its particles can break free and flow as a liquid.

slides.title: Who do you agree with and why?

learners.name: Learner A
learners.statement: Melting and dissolving are the same thing — both make a solid disappear into a liquid.

learners.name: Learner B
learners.statement: They're different. Melting needs heat to change state. Dissolving is mixing with a liquid, not a change of state.

learners.name: Learner C
learners.statement: Both are reversible, so they must be the same kind of change.

slides.title: What temperature does each material melt at?
Is this melting or dissolving?
bullets: MELTING: a solid turns into a liquid when heated — the same material, just a different state.
DISSOLVING: a solid breaks into tiny particles that spread through a liquid — it mixes in, it does not change state.
Misconception: dissolving is NOT a state change — the sugar disappears into water but does not become a gas or a liquid.

Yes, all materials can change their state because...

sections.words: melt  •  boil  •  freeze  •  solid  •  liquid  •  gas  •  melting point  •  temperature  •  evidence  •  for example

sections.text: Yes, all materials can change their state because every material has a melting point at which it changes from solid to liquid. For example, chocolate melts at 34°C, which is why it melts in your hand. Aluminium melts at 660°C and iron at 1538°C, so they need much higher temperatures that we rarely see in daily life. Nitrogen is unusual because it is already a gas at room temperature and only becomes liquid if cooled to -196°C. This shows that all materials can change state, but each needs a very different temperature to do so.
Accept any three materials from the table with correct temperatures.
Award higher marks for: connective "because", named temperatures as evidence, comparison between materials, reference to everyday examples.
